evals.name: command-scenario-spec
evals.prompt: Write the specification for a `RegisterProject(ProjectId Id, string Name)` command that succeeds and appends `ProjectRegistered`, in an application slice. Say where it goes. Give the code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Place it in the slice folder as `<Feature>/<Slice>/when_registering/and_name_is_unique.cs`, wrapped in `#if DEBUG`. Use `CommandScenario<RegisterProject>`, `Execute`, `ShouldBeSuccessful()` and an `async Task` fact using `ShouldHaveAppendedEvent<RegisterProject, ProjectRegistered>(id, predicate)`.
assertions: Places the file in the slice folder under `when_<verb_phrase>/and_<condition>.cs` and wraps it in `#if DEBUG`.
Uses `CommandScenario<RegisterProject>` with `Execute` in `Because` and `ShouldBeSuccessful()`.
Asserts the appended event with `ShouldHaveAppendedEvent<RegisterProject, ProjectRegistered>` taking the event source id and a `Func<TEvent, bool>` predicate, in an `async Task` fact.
Names the facts `should_*` and uses a per-specification identifier such as `ProjectId.New()`.

evals.name: isolated-rejection
evals.prompt: Our rejection spec for 'name is required' builds a command with an empty name and an end date before its start date, and asserts only `ShouldNotBeSuccessful()`. After deleting the name rule the spec is still green. Explain and fix it. Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Each rejection spec violates only the rule it is named after: build the command valid in every other respect so a neighbouring rule cannot make it pass. Assert twice: `ShouldNotBeSuccessful()` and `ShouldHaveValidationErrors()` (or `ShouldHaveValidationErrorBecauseOf(reason)`). Do not assert a message string by default, and run the red check by removing the rule. An unauthorized result is `ShouldNotBeAuthorized()`.
assertions: Explains the spec stays green because the command is invalid in a second way, so another rule produces the error.
Builds the command valid in every other respect and violates only the named rule.
Asserts both `ShouldNotBeSuccessful()` and `ShouldHaveValidationErrors()` (or `ShouldHaveValidationErrorBecauseOf(reason)`), since the first alone cannot tell validation from an exception.
Says not to assert on a message string by default, and to confirm the spec goes red when the rule is removed.

evals.name: plain-call-first
evals.prompt: A command's `Handle()` just computes a price from its input with no read models or pipeline pieces. A teammate wants a CommandScenario for it, and also wants to cover a unique-name constraint in the same CommandScenario. What do you recommend? Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Start a pure decision with a plain method call on the `Specification` base; a direct `Handle()` call does not run validation, authorization, `Provide()` or operations, so keep a scenario for that wiring and appended events. A constraint is enforced at the append, not by the command, so write it with `EventScenario`.
assertions: Recommends a plain method call with the `Specification` base as the default for a pure decision.
Says a direct `Handle()` call does not run validation, authorization, `Provide()` or operations, which is when a CommandScenario earns its place.
Says a constraint violation is written with `EventScenario` because it is enforced at the append and not by the command.
Says the scenario family runs in-process with no HTTP, fixture or server.

evals.name: seed-prior-state
evals.prompt: A command's validator refuses when an injected read model shows the cart already has 3 items. Our rejection spec is green without supplying that state. Do we need events or UseDecisionReads to prove the rule? What if we also need pipeline coverage? Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Prove the validator rule with supplied 3-item state and a passing state; violate only the named rule and confirm it goes red when the rule is removed. Provide acquires data and only short-circuits (ValidationResult/AuthorizationResult) when acquisition yields nothing usable, not for ordinary validation rules. A typed scenario selects decision reads automatically; UseDecisionReads is obsolete. For pipeline proof, an admitted flat model can be pinned for a plain Handle parameter under On; use routed events for per-stream models, advanced DecisionRead parameters or mapping/history proof. Do not assume an unseeded rejection proves the intended rule. Given needs Cratis.Arc.Chronicle.Testing.
assertions: Starts with a direct validator call using explicit failing and passing state; Provide only short-circuits when acquisition yields nothing usable, not for ordinary validation rules.
Does not claim pins are advisory-only: admitted flat plain-parameter reads under On can use pins; per-stream/advanced reads and mapping proof need events.
Warns an unseeded rejection can pass for the wrong reason, isolates the named rule and confirms removing it turns the spec red.
Says typed scenarios select decision reads automatically, UseDecisionReads is obsolete, and Given needs Cratis.Arc.Chronicle.Testing.

evals.name: specify-the-decision-not-the-race
evals.prompt: For ordinary BorrowBook under read protection On, should we simulate two members taking the last copy? Contrast our unusual explicit revision-at-read policy returned in EventsWithConcurrencyScopes. Show the one assembly-level admission spec, explain its blind spots and when AppendConcurrently is legitimate, including its ordering and mode requirements. Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Specify the ordinary business decision from supplied state, not the platform race matrix. Keep one assembly-level DecisionReadAdmissions.ShouldAdmitDecisionReadsIn(typeof(BorrowBook).Assembly) check in Cratis.Arc.Chronicle.Testing.Commands. It checks discovered declarations with declared policy, not explicit body calls or runtime caps; spec-local projections can create ambiguity. Explicit body reads need Admit<T>() or a focused scenario. An unusual application-owned revision-at-read policy can need a focused regression a plain call cannot prove. AppendConcurrently is advanced and explicit-need-only, not routine application guidance: it works with or without decision mode, adds no protection to an unguarded command, queues before execution, runs after response processing before the owner commit, preserves routes and the outer queue, and refuses custom scope factories. Typed scenarios select decision reads automatically; UseDecisionReads is obsolete. Validators own refusals; Provide only short-circuits (ValidationResult/AuthorizationResult) when acquisition yields nothing usable, not for ordinary validation rules.
assertions: Specifies the ordinary last-copy decision with supplied state and no race matrix; allows only a focused regression for the unusual application-owned explicit revision policy.
Shows the assembly-level admission check and namespace; explains declared-policy/discovery limits, explicit body-read checks and spec-local projection ambiguity.
Keeps AppendConcurrently advanced and explicit-need-only, with no decision-mode requirement or added protection; UseDecisionReads is obsolete and typed selection is automatic.
Queues the hook before execution, after-response/before-owner-commit; preserves routes and outer-queue ownership and mentions refusal of custom scope factories.
Does not invent scenario.AppendConditions, require real kernels universally, or weaken production guards; validators own refusals; Provide only short-circuits when acquisition yields nothing usable.
